// Code generated by vandorf. DO NOT EDIT.

package app

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"example.com/app/types"
)

type envGreet struct {
	inGreetGreet inGreetGreet
	outGreetGreet types.GreetArgs
	inGreetRepeat inGreetRepeat
	outGreetRepeat string
}

const (
	pcGreet_GreetGreet = iota
	pcGreet_GreetRepeat
)

// RunGreet runs proc Greet.
func RunGreet(ctx context.Context, name string, times int) (string, error) {
	var zero string
	env := &envGreet{}
	env.inGreetGreet = inGreetGreet{Name: name, Times: times}
	pc := pcGreet_GreetGreet
	for {
		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
			return zero, err
		}
		switch pc {
		case pcGreet_GreetGreet:
			this := types.GreetArgs{Name: env.inGreetGreet.Name, Times: env.inGreetGreet.Times}
			zeroOut(&env.inGreetGreet)
			env.outGreetGreet = this
			env.inGreetRepeat = inGreetRepeat{S: ("hello " + this.Name), N: env.outGreetGreet.Times}
			zeroOut(&env.outGreetGreet)
			pc = pcGreet_GreetRepeat
			continue
		case pcGreet_GreetRepeat:
			this, err := unimplementedGreetRepeat(ctx, env.inGreetRepeat.S, env.inGreetRepeat.N)
			if err != nil {
				return zero, fmt.Errorf("Greet.Repeat: %w", err)
			}
			zeroOut(&env.inGreetRepeat)
			_ = this
			return this, nil
		default:
			return zero, fmt.Errorf("Greet: invalid state %d", pc)
		}
	}
}

	pcMain_MainMain = iota
	pcMain_Greet

	var zero string

	env.inMainMain = inMainMain{}

			return zero, err

		case pcMain_MainMain:

			_ = this

			pc = pcMain_Greet
			continue

			_ = this
			return this, nil

==== /runtime_vandorf.go
// Code generated by vandorf. DO NOT EDIT.

package app

import (
	"cmp"
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"runtime"
	"slices"
	"sync"
	"unsafe"
)

// mapGet looks up k, failing if it's missing.
func mapGet[K comparable, V any](m map[K]V, k K) (V, error) {
	v, ok := m[k]
	if !ok {
		return v, fmt.Errorf("key %v not found", k)
	}
	return v, nil
}

// sliceGet indexes xs, failing if i is out of range.
func sliceGet[E any](xs []E, i int) (E, error) {
	if i < 0 || i >= len(xs) {
		var zero E
		return zero, fmt.Errorf("index %d out of range [0, %d)", i, len(xs))
	}
	return xs[i], nil
}

func mapHas[K comparable, V any](m map[K]V, k K) bool {
	_, ok := m[k]
	return ok
}

// mapKeys returns m's keys in order.
func mapKeys[K cmp.Ordered, V any](m map[K]V) []K {
	ks := make([]K, 0, len(m))
	for k := range m {
		ks = append(ks, k)
	}
	slices.Sort(ks)
	return ks
}

// mapValues returns m's values in key order.
func mapValues[K cmp.Ordered, V any](m map[K]V) []V {
	vs := make([]V, 0, len(m))
	for _, k := range mapKeys(m) {
		vs = append(vs, m[k])
	}
	return vs
}

// mapMerge returns a new map with a's entries and b's, b winning. Maps
// are values in vandorf, so the arguments are never changed.
func mapMerge[K comparable, V any](a, b map[K]V) map[K]V {
	r := make(map[K]V, len(a)+len(b))
	for k, v := range a {
		r[k] = v
	}
	for k, v := range b {
		r[k] = v
	}
	return r
}

// Arrays that sliceConcat builds keep spare capacity in reserve. The
// reserve is hidden from every slice handed out, whose capacity is clipped
// to its length, so code that appends to one (implementations included)
// always copies. reserves records each such array by the address of its
// first element: how much of it is filled. A + whose left side ends
// exactly there appends into the reserve; any other copies. So values
// never change where anyone can see, and a loop like acc + [x] costs
// amortized O(1) per element. A finalizer drops an array's entry when it's
// freed, before its address can be reused.
type reserve struct{ filled, cap int }

var (
	reservesMu sync.Mutex
	reserves   = map[uintptr]reserve{}
)

// sliceConcat returns a new slice with a's elements, then b's; neither
// changes.
func sliceConcat[E any](a, b []E) []E {
	n := len(a) + len(b)
	var zero E
	size := int(unsafe.Sizeof(zero))
	if size == 0 {
		// All zero-size arrays share one address: nothing to reserve.
		return make([]E, n)
	}
	if p := unsafe.SliceData(a); p != nil {
		base := uintptr(unsafe.Pointer(p))
		reservesMu.Lock()
		if r, ok := reserves[base]; ok && r.filled == len(a) && n <= r.cap {
			reserves[base] = reserve{n, r.cap}
			reservesMu.Unlock()
			full := unsafe.Slice(p, r.cap)
			copy(full[len(a):n], b)
			return full[:n:n]
		}
		reservesMu.Unlock()
	}
	// Room to double, and over 16 bytes: the tiny allocator's blocks may
	// never be finalized.
	c := max(2*n, 16/size+1)
	r := make([]E, n, c)
	copy(r, a)
	copy(r[len(a):], b)
	p := unsafe.SliceData(r)
	base := uintptr(unsafe.Pointer(p))
	reservesMu.Lock()
	reserves[base] = reserve{n, c}
	reservesMu.Unlock()
	runtime.SetFinalizer(p, func(*E) {
		reservesMu.Lock()
		delete(reserves, base)
		reservesMu.Unlock()
	})
	return r[:n:n]
}

// mapRemove returns a new map without the keys ks.
func mapRemove[K comparable, V any](m map[K]V, ks []K) map[K]V {
	r := make(map[K]V, len(m))
	for k, v := range m {
		r[k] = v
	}
	for _, k := range ks {
		delete(r, k)
	}
	return r
}

// ptrTo boxes a value, for fields that would otherwise make a type contain
// itself.
func ptrTo[T any](v T) *T {
	return &v
}

// zeroOut clears a slot no later state reads, so the garbage collector can
// reclaim what it held.
func zeroOut[T any](p *T) {
	var zero T
	*p = zero
}

// joinAll runs fs concurrently and waits for all of them: a spawn's joined
// branches. The first error cancels the rest and is returned.
func joinAll(ctx context.Context, fs ...func(context.Context) error) error {
	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
	defer cancel()
	var (
		wg    sync.WaitGroup
		once  sync.Once
		first error
	)
	for _, f := range fs {
		wg.Add(1)
		go func() {
			defer wg.Done()
			if err := f(ctx); err != nil {
				once.Do(func() { first = err; cancel() })
			}
		}()
	}
	wg.Wait()
	return first
}

// spawnDetached runs f on a goroutine of its own, a spawn's detached branch:
// nothing waits for it, it outlives ctx's cancellation, and a failure is
// only reported.
func spawnDetached(ctx context.Context, f func(context.Context) error) {
	ctx = context.WithoutCancel(ctx)
	go func() {
		if err := f(ctx); err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "error: %v\n", err)
		}
	}()
}

// fanOut runs f over xs concurrently and returns the results in input order.
// The first error cancels the remaining elements.
func fanOut[E, R any](ctx context.Context, xs []E, f func(context.Context, E) (R, error)) ([]R, error) {
	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
	defer cancel()
	out := make([]R, len(xs))
	var (
		wg    sync.WaitGroup
		once  sync.Once
		first error
	)
	for i, x := range xs {
		wg.Add(1)
		go func() {
			defer wg.Done()
			r, err := f(ctx, x)
			if err != nil {
				once.Do(func() { first = err; cancel() })
				return
			}
			out[i] = r
		}()
	}
	wg.Wait()
	return out, first
}

// mapRemove returns a new map without the keys ks.
func mapRemove[K comparable, V any](m map[K]V, ks []K) map[K]V {
	r := make(map[K]V, len(m))
	for k, v := range m {
		r[k] = v

// joinAll runs fs concurrently and waits for all of them: a spawn's joined
// branches. The first error cancels the rest and is returned.
func joinAll(ctx context.Context, fs ...func(context.Context) error) error {
	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
	defer cancel()

		wg    sync.WaitGroup
		once  sync.Once
		first error
	)
	for _, f := range fs {
		wg.Add(1)
		go func() {
			defer wg.Done()
			if err := f(ctx); err != nil {
				once.Do(func() { first = err; cancel() })
			}
		}()
	}
	wg.Wait()
	return first
}

// spawnDetached runs f on a goroutine of its own, a spawn's detached branch:
// nothing waits for it, it outlives ctx's cancellation, and a failure is
// only reported.
func spawnDetached(ctx context.Context, f func(context.Context) error) {

	go func() {
		if err := f(ctx); err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "error: %v\n", err)
		}
	}()
}

// fanOut runs f over xs concurrently and returns the results in input order.
// The first error cancels the remaining elements.
func fanOut[E, R any](ctx context.Context, xs []E, f func(context.Context, E) (R, error)) ([]R, error) {
	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
	defer cancel()
	out := make([]R, len(xs))
	var (
		wg    sync.WaitGroup
		once  sync.Once
		first error
	)
	for i, x := range xs {
		wg.Add(1)
		go func() {
			defer wg.Done()
			r, err := f(ctx, x)
			if err != nil {
				once.Do(func() { first = err; cancel() })
				return
			}
			out[i] = r
		}()
	}
	wg.Wait()
	return out, first
}

	outMainMain types.MainArgs
	inGreet inGreetGreet
	outGreet string
}

const (
	pcMain_MainMain = iota
	pcMain_Greet
)

// RunMain runs proc Main.
func RunMain(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
	var zero string
	env := &envMain{}
	env.inMainMain = inMainMain{}
	pc := pcMain_MainMain
	for {
		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
			return zero, err
		}
		switch pc {
		case pcMain_MainMain:
			this := types.MainArgs{}
			zeroOut(&env.inMainMain)
			_ = this
			env.inGreet = inGreetGreet{Name: "x", Times: 2}
			pc = pcMain_Greet
			continue
		case pcMain_Greet:
			this, err := RunGreet(ctx, env.inGreet.Name, env.inGreet.Times)
			if err != nil {
				return zero, fmt.Errorf("Greet: %w", err)
			}
			zeroOut(&env.inGreet)
			_ = this
			return this, nil
		default:
			return zero, fmt.Errorf("Main: invalid state %d", pc)
		}
	}
}


==== /runtime_vandorf.go
// Code generated by vandorf. DO NOT EDIT.

package main

import (
	"cmp"
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"runtime"
	"slices"
	"sync"
	"unsafe"
)

// mapGet looks up k, failing if it's missing.
func mapGet[K comparable, V any](m map[K]V, k K) (V, error) {
	v, ok := m[k]
	if !ok {
		return v, fmt.Errorf("key %v not found", k)
	}
	return v, nil
}

// sliceGet indexes xs, failing if i is out of range.
func sliceGet[E any](xs []E, i int) (E, error) {
	if i < 0 || i >= len(xs) {
		var zero E
		return zero, fmt.Errorf("index %d out of range [0, %d)", i, len(xs))
	}
	return xs[i], nil
}

func mapHas[K comparable, V any](m map[K]V, k K) bool {
	_, ok := m[k]
	return ok
}

// mapKeys returns m's keys in order.
func mapKeys[K cmp.Ordered, V any](m map[K]V) []K {
	ks := make([]K, 0, len(m))
	for k := range m {
		ks = append(ks, k)
	}
	slices.Sort(ks)
	return ks
}

// mapValues returns m's values in key order.
func mapValues[K cmp.Ordered, V any](m map[K]V) []V {
	vs := make([]V, 0, len(m))
	for _, k := range mapKeys(m) {
		vs = append(vs, m[k])
	}
	return vs
}

// mapMerge returns a new map with a's entries and b's, b winning. Maps
// are values in vandorf, so the arguments are never changed.
func mapMerge[K comparable, V any](a, b map[K]V) map[K]V {
	r := make(map[K]V, len(a)+len(b))
	for k, v := range a {
		r[k] = v
	}
	for k, v := range b {
		r[k] = v
	}
	return r
}

// Arrays that sliceConcat builds keep spare capacity in reserve. The
// reserve is hidden from every slice handed out, whose capacity is clipped
// to its length, so code that appends to one (implementations included)
// always copies. reserves records each such array by the address of its
// first element: how much of it is filled. A + whose left side ends
// exactly there appends into the reserve; any other copies. So values
// never change where anyone can see, and a loop like acc + [x] costs
// amortized O(1) per element. A finalizer drops an array's entry when it's
// freed, before its address can be reused.
type reserve struct{ filled, cap int }

var (
	reservesMu sync.Mutex
	reserves   = map[uintptr]reserve{}
)

// sliceConcat returns a new slice with a's elements, then b's; neither
// changes.
func sliceConcat[E any](a, b []E) []E {
	n := len(a) + len(b)
	var zero E
	size := int(unsafe.Sizeof(zero))
	if size == 0 {
		// All zero-size arrays share one address: nothing to reserve.
		return make([]E, n)
	}
	if p := unsafe.SliceData(a); p != nil {
		base := uintptr(unsafe.Pointer(p))
		reservesMu.Lock()
		if r, ok := reserves[base]; ok && r.filled == len(a) && n <= r.cap {
			reserves[base] = reserve{n, r.cap}
			reservesMu.Unlock()
			full := unsafe.Slice(p, r.cap)
			copy(full[len(a):n], b)
			return full[:n:n]
		}
		reservesMu.Unlock()
	}
	// Room to double, and over 16 bytes: the tiny allocator's blocks may
	// never be finalized.
	c := max(2*n, 16/size+1)
	r := make([]E, n, c)
	copy(r, a)
	copy(r[len(a):], b)
	p := unsafe.SliceData(r)
	base := uintptr(unsafe.Pointer(p))
	reservesMu.Lock()
	reserves[base] = reserve{n, c}
	reservesMu.Unlock()
	runtime.SetFinalizer(p, func(*E) {
		reservesMu.Lock()
		delete(reserves, base)
		reservesMu.Unlock()
	})
	return r[:n:n]
}

// mapRemove returns a new map without the keys ks.
func mapRemove[K comparable, V any](m map[K]V, ks []K) map[K]V {
	r := make(map[K]V, len(m))
	for k, v := range m {
		r[k] = v
	}
	for _, k := range ks {
		delete(r, k)
	}
	return r
}

// ptrTo boxes a value, for fields that would otherwise make a type contain
// itself.
func ptrTo[T any](v T) *T {
	return &v
}

// zeroOut clears a slot no later state reads, so the garbage collector can
// reclaim what it held.
func zeroOut[T any](p *T) {
	var zero T
	*p = zero
}

// joinAll runs fs concurrently and waits for all of them: a spawn's joined
// branches. The first error cancels the rest and is returned.
func joinAll(ctx context.Context, fs ...func(context.Context) error) error {
	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
	defer cancel()
	var (
		wg    sync.WaitGroup
		once  sync.Once
		first error
	)
	for _, f := range fs {
		wg.Add(1)
		go func() {
			defer wg.Done()
			if err := f(ctx); err != nil {
				once.Do(func() { first = err; cancel() })
			}
		}()
	}
	wg.Wait()
	return first
}

// spawnDetached runs f on a goroutine of its own, a spawn's detached branch:
// nothing waits for it, it outlives ctx's cancellation, and a failure is
// only reported.
func spawnDetached(ctx context.Context, f func(context.Context) error) {
	ctx = context.WithoutCancel(ctx)
	go func() {
		if err := f(ctx); err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "error: %v\n", err)
		}
	}()
}

// fanOut runs f over xs concurrently and returns the results in input order.
// The first error cancels the remaining elements.
func fanOut[E, R any](ctx context.Context, xs []E, f func(context.Context, E) (R, error)) ([]R, error) {
	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
	defer cancel()
	out := make([]R, len(xs))
	var (
		wg    sync.WaitGroup
		once  sync.Once
		first error
	)
	for i, x := range xs {
		wg.Add(1)
		go func() {
			defer wg.Done()
			r, err := f(ctx, x)
			if err != nil {
				once.Do(func() { first = err; cancel() })
				return
			}
			out[i] = r
		}()
	}
	wg.Wait()
	return out, first
}

// Code generated by vandorf. DO NOT EDIT.

// Command bin runs proc Greet, taking its parameters as arguments.
//
//	usage: bin <name: string> <times: int>
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"strconv"
	procs "example.com/app"
)

const usage = "usage: bin <name: string> <times: int>"

func main() {
	if len(os.Args) != 3 {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, usage)
		os.Exit(2)
	}
	argName := os.Args[1]
	argTimes, err := strconv.Atoi(os.Args[2])
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "times: %v\n%s\n", err, usage)
		os.Exit(2)
	}
	result, err := procs.RunGreet(context.Background(), argName, argTimes)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "error:", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	fmt.Println(result)
}
